test_title: SSC CPO Tier-II Previous Year Paper (Held On: 8th November 2021)
subject: general
question:
**Select the most appropriate indirect form of the given sentence.**

Pauline said to Cornelius, “Will Mr. Vincent be coming for dinner on Thursday evening?”

options.text: Pauline wanted to know from Cornelius if Mr. Vincent is coming for dinner on Thursday evening.
Pauline said to Cornelius will Mr. Vincent be coming for dinner on Thursday evening.
Pauline asked Cornelius if Mr. Vincent would be coming for dinner on Thursday evening.
Pauline told Cornelius that Mr. Vincent would be coming for dinner on Thursday evening.

solution:
The correct answer is- 'Pauline asked Cornelius if Mr Vincent would be coming for dinner on Thursday evening.'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• To change the sentence to an indirect speech we need to follow the following steps:

 
 
• As the reported speech is an **interrogative sentence**, so **said **will change to **asked**.
 
• The inverted commas of reported speech should be replaced with the **conjunction ***if*.
 
• As the reported speech is in the **Future continuous, **it will change to the **Conditional continuous**.
 
 
• **Direct**: *She said, “I **will be **going to Scotland tomorrow.”*
 
• **​Indirect**: *She said that she **would be **going to Scotland the next day.*
 
 
 
 
 
• Thus according to the given steps, *option 3 *is the correct answer.

And the correct sentence is: *Pauline asked Cornelius if Mr Vincent would be coming for dinner on Thursday evening.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• Let's understand how to convert the sentence **into indirect speech **if the reported speech is an **interrogative sentence**.

 
 
• If a direct speech sentence begins with an **auxiliary verb**/**helping verb**, the joining clause should be **if **or **whether**

 
 
• **Example:** 

 
 
• **Direct**: *She said, "Will you come to the party?"*
 
• **Indirect**: *She asked whether we would come to the party.*
 
 
 
 
 
• Reporting verbs such as ‘**said/ said to**’ changes to *enquired*, *asked*, or *demanded*.
 
 
• Example:
 
 
• **​Direct**: *He said to me, "What are you wearing?"*
 
• **Indirect**: *He asked me what I was wearing.*
